hints: Because the denominator has three distinct linear factors, use one constant numerator over each factor.
Substitute the zeros \(x=-\tfrac12,\tfrac12,-2\) to determine the three constants efficiently.
walkthrough:
State the given rational expression:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{2 + 11x - 10x^2}{(1 + 2x)(1 - 2x)(2 + x)}$$

Notice that the degree of the numerator polynomial is $2$ and the degree of the denominator polynomial is $3$. Since the degree of the numerator is strictly less than the degree of the denominator, this is a proper fraction with three distinct linear factors in the denominator.

Set up the partial fractions decomposition with unknown constants $A, B, C$:
$$\dfrac{2 + 11x - 10x^2}{(1 + 2x)(1 - 2x)(2 + x)} = \dfrac{A}{1 + 2x} + \dfrac{B}{1 - 2x} + \dfrac{C}{2 + x}$$

Multiply both sides by the common denominator $(1 + 2x)(1 - 2x)(2 + x)$ to clear fractions:
$$2 + 11x - 10x^2 = A(1 - 2x)(2 + x) + B(1 + 2x)(2 + x) + C(1 + 2x)(1 - 2x)$$

Determine constant $A$ by substituting $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ (the zero of $1 + 2x$):
$$\text{LHS} = 2 + 11\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 10\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 2 - \dfrac{11}{2} - 10\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 2 - \dfrac{11}{2} - \dfrac{5}{2} = 2 - \dfrac{16}{2} = 2 - 8 = -6$$
$$\text{RHS} = A\left(1 - 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + B(0) + C(0) = A(1 + 1)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = A(2)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 3A$$
Equating both sides gives:
$$3A = -6 \implies A = -2$$

Determine constant $B$ by substituting $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (the zero of $1 - 2x$):
$$\text{LHS} = 2 + 11\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 10\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 2 + \dfrac{11}{2} - 10\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 2 + \dfrac{11}{2} - \dfrac{5}{2} = 2 + \dfrac{6}{2} = 2 + 3 = 5$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(0) + B\left(1 + 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + C(0) = B(1 + 1)\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = B(2)\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = 5B$$
Equating both sides gives:
$$5B = 5 \implies B = 1$$

Determine constant $C$ by substituting $x = -2$ (the zero of $2 + x$):
$$\text{LHS} = 2 + 11(-2) - 10(-2)^2 = 2 - 22 - 10(4) = -20 - 40 = -60$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(0) + B(0) + C(1 + 2(-2))(1 - 2(-2)) = C(1 - 4)(1 + 4) = C(-3)(5) = -15C$$
Equating both sides gives:
$$-15C = -60 \implies C = \dfrac{-60}{-15} = 4$$

Substitute the values $A = -2$, $B = 1$, and $C = 4$ into the partial fraction decomposition:
$$f(x) = -\dfrac{2}{1 + 2x} + \dfrac{1}{1 - 2x} + \dfrac{4}{2 + x}$$

hints: Expand each partial fraction from part (a) using the geometric/binomial series \((1+u)^{-1}=1-u+u^2+\cdots\).
For the \((2+x)^{-1}\) term, first factor out 2 so that the bracket is \(1+\tfrac12x\).
Keep terms only through \(x^2\), multiply by the partial-fraction constants, and collect like powers.
walkthrough:
State the partial fraction decomposition from part (a):
$$f(x) = -2(1 + 2x)^{-1} + (1 - 2x)^{-1} + 4(2 + x)^{-1}$$

Recall the binomial series expansion for $(1 + u)^{-1}$:
$$(1 + u)^{-1} = 1 - u + u^2 - u^3 + \cdots \quad \text{for } |u| < 1$$

Expand the third term $4(2 + x)^{-1}$:
Factor out $2$ from $(2 + x)$ to match standard form $(1 + u)^{-1}$:
$$4(2 + x)^{-1} = 4\left[2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]^{-1} = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1} = 2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1}$$
Apply the binomial series with $u = \dfrac{x}{2}$:
$$\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1} = 1 - \dfrac{x}{2} + \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 - \cdots = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{4}x^2$$
$$2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1} = 2\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{4}x^2\right) = 2 - x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$$

Sum the three expansions together to obtain the expansion of $f(x)$ up to the term in $x^2$:
$$f(x) = (-2 + 4x - 8x^2) + (1 + 2x + 4x^2) + \left(2 - x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right)$$

Combine all terms to state the final expansion:
$$f(x) = 1 + 5x - \dfrac{7}{2}x^2$$
